name: Google Play service account
description: A Google Cloud service account invited into Play Console with access to this app, its JSON key stored in Infisical.

spec.summary: A service account the Play Developer API accepts for this app: created in Google Cloud, invited into Play Console with the permissions the scripts need, and its JSON key kept only in Infisical.

params.label: Android package name
params.description: The applicationId: android.package in app.json, e.g. com.example.app.

params.label: Google Cloud project id
params.description: The project the service account is created in (its id, not its display name).

params.label: Secret name in Infisical
params.description: Where the JSON key is stored. Scripts read the key from this secret.

instructions.*:
Enter the app's package name — `android.package` in `app.json`, or `applicationId` in `android/app/build.gradle`.

The app must **already exist in Play Console** (*Home → Create app*), and Google only lets the API edit an app after **its first bundle was uploaded by hand** (any track, internal testing is fine). A brand-new app answers the API with *Package not found* until then.

steps.title: Pick a Google Cloud project and enable the API

instructions.*:
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate to create a project, or reuse one you already have for this app. Copy its **project id** (shown under the name in the project picker — not the display name).
2. Enable the **Google Play Android Developer API** in it: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/androidpublisher.googleapis.com — pick the project at the top and press **Enable**.
3. Enter the project id here and press **Check**.

The project does not need to be linked to Play Console for this to work; the service account is invited into Play Console by email in a later step.

steps.title: Create the service account and its JSON key

instructions.*:
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/serviceaccounts?project={{gcpProjectId}} and press **Create service account**.
2. Name it after what uses it (for example `play-automation`), press **Create and continue**, and **grant it no Google Cloud role** — its permissions come from Play Console, not from Cloud IAM. Press **Done**.
3. Copy the service account's **email** (`…@{{gcpProjectId}}.iam.gserviceaccount.com`): the next step invites it.
4. Open the account, go to **Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON → Create**. A `.json` file downloads **once**: keep it where you can find it for a few minutes — the step after next uploads it to Infisical, and then you delete it.

If key creation is blocked by an organisation policy (`iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`), an organisation admin has to allow it for this project first.

Press **Done** when you have the file.

steps.title: Invite it into Play Console with the right permissions
Store the JSON key in Infisical

instructions.*:
Drop the `.json` key downloaded two steps ago. It goes straight from this page to Infisical as **{{playServiceAccountSecret}}** in {{infisicalProject}} / {{infisicalEnv}}; nothing else keeps a copy.

Then **delete the downloaded file** (and empty the trash): the copy that matters is now the one in Infisical, and a key file lying in Downloads is how keys leak.
